item.title: I have never been more livid.
item.description: We got text messages at 7am that someone had our lost cat, Coco. They sent several pictures and claimed they found her on the side of the road in our neighborhood while visiting a friend and took her home. They said that they already spent $100 on her getting a kennel and cat bed and if we wanted her back we had to Apple Pay or chime them the money, they would not bring her to us without sending it first. I knew something was wrong, starting with being able to “pick her up on the side of the road”, she would never let anyone but us touch her and she is fast. So I put the images through an Ai detector and they came back 95% positive for Ai. If I could find this person I would probably got to prison. How fucking low can you be as a person to do something like that! In other news, thank you to everyone for your suggestions. We have the litter box and her personal items outside where they can’t get rained on and we have some clothes outside. Flyers are up and my wife has plastered info all over FB and Nextdoor and we finally got the original info for her chip. Hopefully we will get some real info soon.

item.title: GovBrief Today #570
item.description: Dr. Oz took three questions on Face the Nation to say a childhood vaccine will not kill your child. Donald Trump called the 55-year-old MMR vaccine "quite lethal" two weeks ago. Asked to clarify, his Medicaid administrator answered questions about parental rights. The third time he was asked, he said the vaccine is not lethal. On the same broadcast, a Republican congressman running for governor of Florida blamed the measles outbreak on "rampant illegal immigration." Florida's kindergarten vaccination rate has already fallen below herd immunity. So has the country's, as measles spreads at 35-year highs. Neither man named the president. After I tucked them under her wing and she felt them move she accepted they were her babies. Even though she sat on no eggs for 2 months. She had raised strong babies before. Lets hope her adopted brood becomes just as independent
